about: The components of @acaprino/sigrid, written from its source by scripts/agents.mjs. Each entry is a level of the package (the main entry holds what does not draw; then `/primitives`, `/components`, `/layout`, `/assemblies`, and the assemblies with an entry of their own): a name is imported from the entry it is listed under. `about` is the comment at the head of a file, `doc` the comment on a component. `props` are the props the toolkit declares; `passesOn` says the component also takes the props of the element or the part it draws. `types` are the object types those props are made of (a column, a notice, an option), with their fields. `also` are the other names the file exports: helpers, constants, types. `fromLibraries` are parts of Ark UI or Base UI the entry hands on unchanged.

files.about:
A theme from two colours (owner, 2026-11-22: «due colori e poi un accento»): the theme colour sets the buttons, the
selection, the links and the focus ring; the spot colour is the accent, the one loud colour, kept for the few things
that ask for attention now. The grays of the page are the third, quiet colour. The spot is not picked from the whole
wheel: three colours that go with the theme colour are proposed, from quiet to loud, and the engine then moves each
one until its contrast thresholds hold.

types.name: ColorThemePick
types.doc: What a colour theme is made from.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The theme colour, `#rrggbb`.

fields.name: spot
fields.doc: The spot colour: one of the three proposals, or a colour of the user's own (`#rrggbb`). Absent: no spot.

files.about:
The eighteen free colors (for what the user colours: a folder, a group, a mark), in hue order (from red to pink). They are medium tints: the color is
user data, the same in both themes, so it holds up on both the light and the dark paper. An app that keeps the list
elsewhere too (on its server) keeps the same hex values there. A color that is already saved never falls out of the list.

Density: how tall the controls are, how much side padding they have and how much room a list row takes. Like the
themes it is data: the toolkit ships three presets (`DENSITIES`) and an app may pass a definition of its own, or a
preset with some measures changed (`densityWith`). `applyDensity` writes the measures on an element as CSS variables
(`--density-*`) and the id as `data-density`; `styles/theme.css` turns them into the tokens the components use
(`--control-md`, `--pad-md`, `--row-height`…), with `normal` as the value before any script runs and 44px as the
floor of every control and row with a coarse pointer.

files.about:
A theme from two colours, and the accents that go with a base colour (owner, 2026-11-22: «due colori: la base, che
di suo è il bianco ma si può cambiare, portata sulle tonalità chiarissime, e un accento scelto con i principi della
colorimetria, suggerito in automatico»).
- The base is the page. Whatever colour is chosen, only its hue stays: it is brought to a very light tone (an OKLCH
  lightness of 0.985 and a chroma of 0.018 at most), so the page is a white with a breath of that colour and the text
  keeps its contrast. No base, or a gray one, is the neutral white. In dark the same hue is a very dark tone.
- The accent is what the eye is led by (R2). It is not picked from the whole wheel: from the base's hue the classical
  harmonies give the hues that go with it, all on one wheel, OKLCH's, where equal turns are equal steps for the eye:
  the split complement (150° to either side), the complement (180°), the triad (120°), the neighbours (30°) and the
  base's own hue. Each is drawn at the lightness and saturation of a button, inside what a screen can show.
- They are ranked. A split complement comes first: it is clearly another colour without the vibration of the exact
  opposite. A hue that would read as the red of an error is moved out of its room and ranked lower, and one beside
  the green of success or the amber of a warning loses a little: an accent must never be taken for a status. A hue
  between yellow and lime loses more: yellow is itself only when it is light, and at the lightness a button needs
  under its label it turns to olive.
A white or gray base has no hue to start from: the proposals are then eight hues spread round the wheel, the blue
first. The theme engine then moves every colour until its contrast thresholds hold, as for any theme.

fields.name: id
fields.doc: Stable for a base: `split+150`, `mono`, `spread-264`.

fields.name: turn
fields.doc: How far round the wheel from the base's hue, in degrees. Zero for `mono` and for `spread`.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: The accent, `#rrggbb`.

fields.name: recommended
fields.doc: The first of the list: what the toolkit would choose.

fields.name: moved
fields.doc: The hue fell in the red of errors and was moved out of it.

types.name: DuoPick
types.doc: What a theme of two colours is made from.

fields.name: base
fields.doc: The base: the colour of the page, brought to a very light tone. Absent, null or a gray: the neutral white.

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent, `#rrggbb`: one of `accentSuggestions(base)`, or a colour of the user's own.

files.about:
The height of what the person sees, whatever hosts the page: a browser tab with its bars showing or gone, a Custom
Tab, an installed app, a web view, a window half-snapped, with the keyboard open or shut. `100vh` is the height with
the browser's bars gone, so a page that fits it still scrolls; `100dvh` follows the bars in most hosts but not in
all, and never the keyboard. `visualViewport` is what the browser itself says it shows: its height, taken back to
layout pixels with its scale (a page pinched in would otherwise read shorter). Where there is no `visualViewport`,
the window's height.
`useAppHeight` writes it in px as `--app-height` on the root (theme.css: `100dvh` until a script writes it, and where
none does), and again when the visible area changes (the bars sliding, the keyboard, a rotation, a window resized):
many events in one frame are one write. `AppShell` runs it by itself. Any number of parts may run it: they share one
listener, and the property goes when the last of them stops. On a server it does nothing.

What makes a page behave as the window of a program and not as a page in a browser. An app that runs in a window of
its own (no address bar, no browser around it) calls `useDesktopGuard()` once; in a browser tab it does not.
- The keys a browser engine keeps for itself do nothing: reload, print, find, history, the page's source, the
  developer tools, back and forward (with Ctrl, or with Command on a Mac). They are refused in the capture phase and not stopped, so the app's own handler
  for the same key (Ctrl+F for its search, Ctrl+S in its editor) still runs.
- The engine's own menu on a right press is refused, except where it is useful: in a field (it offers editing) and
  over selected text (Copy). An app's own context menu is not touched: it shows its own.
- The back and forward buttons of a mouse do not navigate.
- A picture or a link is not dragged out of the window, unless the app made it draggable.
`ownKeysIn` names the places that run their own keys and menus (a terminal, a code editor): there nothing is refused.
The technique is the one Imago's windows use (its `guardDesktop`); this is the toolkit's own writing of it. The
native side of the same guard (navigation limited to the app's origin, new windows refused) is the app's host.

fields.name: ownKeysIn
fields.doc: A selector for the places that keep the engine's keys and menu: `'.xterm, .cm-editor'`.

files.about:
What a drag brings in, already read: files, a link or text. Only one, in this order of precedence: a drag with
files and text (an email from Outlook: the file and its subject) is made of files. Several addresses together are
text, one per line. Whether a file is an email is decided by whoever receives it.

types.name: AttachPayload
types.doc: What becomes an attachment: files or a link (text is not an attachment).

types.name: DropPayload
types.doc: What a drag brings in, already read: files, a link or text. Only one, in this order of precedence: a drag with files and text (an email from Outlook: the file and its subject) is made of files. Several addresses together are text, one per line. Whether a file is an email is decided by whoever receives it.

fields.name: props
fields.type: { onDragStart: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDragEnd: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDragOver: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDragLeave: (e: DragEvent) => void; onDrop: (e: DragEvent) => void; }

files.about: A row that scrolls sideways by itself while something is dragged near its left or right edge.
Kind of an item of the stack.
The text of a capture input as lines: a non-empty line is a thing, spaces at the edges do not count.

A small Markdown of our own, for a title and the notes under it. No dependencies and no `innerHTML`: the text becomes
React elements, so a `<script>` written in a note stays text. Links are not opened from here (the app that uses the
package does it): they are shown underlined, with the address as a hint.

Inline (title and notes): **bold** or __bold__, *italic* or _italic_, ~~strikethrough~~, `code`, [text](url).
In blocks (notes only): lines starting with «- », «* » or «1. » (lists), «- [ ] » and «- [x] » (checkboxes, read-only),
«# » (heading), «> » (quote); an empty line separates paragraphs. A «\*» stays an asterisk.
Below this point the sidebar is a drawer or, with the tabs, a page: the same `md` as `theme.css` (860px).

Optional animations: only in response to a gesture, under 250 ms, off by default. A component animates
when MotionProvider or the control enables it and the system allows motion. Motion lives in a separate chunk
(`motion-impl`), loaded the first time it is needed: with animations off it never even reaches the browser.

components.name: MotionProvider
components.doc: Enable motion for a subtree, including its portals. Individual controls can override the preference. While at least one provider has motion on, the document root carries `data-motion`: with it (and only where the system allows motion) a control's fill, border and text ease to the state under the pointer instead of snapping (theme.css).

types.name: MotionImpl
types.doc: The Motion chunk's module: what `useMotion` returns when a component animates.

fields.name: NoticeCard
fields.type: ({ y, enter, still, leaving, beyond, ...props }: Omit<HTMLMotionProps<"div">, "initial" | "animate" | "exit" | "transition"> & { y: number; enter: boolean; still?: boolean; leaving: NoticeLeaving; be…
fields.doc: A notice of the column: the same `<div>` as without animations, moved by Motion to its place (`y`). `enter` false for a notice that was already there at mount: it does not come in animated (INV-002). `still` while such a notice is being put in its place for the first time (its height and the others' are measured after it mounts): it is simply put there, it does not glide. `beyond` is the place above the last one, where a pushed-out notice goes.

fields.name: Notices
fields.doc: Motion's features for `NoticeCard`: the column is rendered by Ark's `Toaster`, so the provider goes around it.

fields.name: Presence
fields.type: ({ children, pop }: { children: ReactNode; pop?: boolean; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: The elements with an exit animation. `initial={false}`: what is already there at mount does not move (no animation on load). `reducedMotion="user"`: a second defense besides `useMotion`.

fields.name: ListItem
fields.type: ({ ref, enter, className, children }: { ref?: React.Ref<HTMLLIElement>; enter: boolean; className?: string; children: (leaving: boolean) => ReactNode; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: An item of an animated list, direct child of `Presence pop` (it passes the `ref` on: `popLayout` measures it). `enter` false for what was already there or arrived with the first load: it does not come in animated (INV-002). While it leaves it is `inert` and `children` is told so.

fields.name: Leaving
fields.doc: Tells whether the child of `Presence` it sits in is leaving. A removed notice or item stays in the DOM for the duration of the exit (100-200 ms) with the handlers of the last render: whoever uses it must make the element inert (`inert`) and not let clicks through, otherwise a double click on «Cancel» or «Sort» would act twice.

fields.name: popCheck
fields.doc: The mark of a Checkbox just checked: stamped once, growing from half its size as it fades in.

fields.name: enterSheet
fields.doc: The panel enters from its own edge. Its swipe transform remains under the finger.

fields.name: enterPopup
fields.doc: The card of a menu or popover opening: it fades in, coming a few pixels from the side of its button. `anchor` is that button, for a caller whose positioning library does not tell the side in time: the side is then measured.

fields.name: landCard
fields.doc: The card just placed in a column of the board: it comes down a little into its place, only once.

fields.name: throwCard
fields.type: (el: Element, direction: "left" | "right") => { done: Promise<void>; release: () => void; }
fields.doc: A card of a deck thrown to the side it was decided to: it goes on from where the finger left it, by its own width, and fades, gathering speed as what leaves does. It stays out (`release` puts it back) until the deck has drawn the next card, so the card thrown is never seen at rest again. `done` always resolves.

fields.name: pressable
fields.type: (el: HTMLElement, { hoverScale, tapScale }?: { hoverScale?: number; tapScale?: number; }) => () => void
fields.doc: Press feedback on the existing `<button>`: the scale of `tapScale` while pressed (`MOTION.press`), back when released (`MOTION.release`); the scale of `hoverScale` under the pointer, when an app asks for one. With the default hover nothing listens to the pointer and nothing is written on the element until it is pressed. Returns the cleanup, which also stops a movement still running. A disabled button does not move.

fields.name: enterTooltip
fields.doc: A hint appearing: it fades in a few pixels from its button, quickly, so it never trails the pointer.

fields.name: Highlight
fields.type: ({ id, className }: { id: string; className?: string; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: The pill under the chosen item of a group. Rendered inside the chosen item only; when the choice changes Motion carries it from the old item to the new one (`layoutId`). On mount it is simply there.

fields.name: Turn
fields.type: ({ open, children }: { open: boolean; children: ReactNode; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: One arrow that turns a quarter when its group opens.

fields.name: HoverHighlight
fields.type: ({ container, selector, className }: { container: HTMLElement | null; selector: string; className?: string; }) => React.JSX.Element
fields.doc: One hover background for the whole container: it appears at once on the first row, glides with the mouse from row to row (`MOTION.follow`) and fades when the pointer leaves. Only its transform moves: it takes the place and the size of the new row at once, and is carried there from where and how large it was seen (a translation from the container's corner, a scale from its own). So it also glides between rows of different heights, without animating a size. The rows are found by `selector` (delegation: no handler per row); `container` must be positioned. Mouse only: a finger has no hover. It never takes the pointer from the rows under it.

fields.name: m
fields.type: (<Props, TagName extends keyof DOMMotionComponents | string = "div">(Component: TagName | string | React.ComponentType<Props>, { forwardMotionProps, type }?: MotionComponentOptions, preloadedFeatures…

fields.name: FLUENT_DURATIONS
fields.type: { readonly faster: 100; readonly fast: 150; readonly normal: 200; }
fields.doc: Fluent 2's duration tokens, in milliseconds (`@fluentui/tokens`, `durationFaster`, `durationFast`, `durationNormal`): the ones under 250 ms that the toolkit uses. The values are Fluent's, unchanged.

fields.name: FLUENT_CURVES
fields.type: { readonly decelerateMid: readonly [0, 0, 0, 1]; readonly accelerateMin: readonly [0.8, 0, 0.78, 1]; readonly easyEase: readonly [0.33, 0, 0.67, 1]; }
fields.doc: Fluent 2's curve tokens, as the control points of a cubic Bézier (`@fluentui/tokens`, `curveDecelerateMid`, `curveAccelerateMid`, `curveEasyEase`): the ones the toolkit uses. The values are Fluent's, unchanged. None leaves 0..1: nothing overshoots.

fields.name: DURATION_MS
fields.type: { readonly toast: 200; readonly mark: 100; readonly sheet: 200; readonly row: 200; readonly popup: 150; readonly land: 150; }
fields.doc: Durations in milliseconds of what enters or leaves once: all under 250 ms (test/animated.test.tsx). `toast` is how long a notice that leaves the column stays in the DOM (Ark's `removeDelay`): longer than its exit (`GESTURE_MS.leave`).

fields.name: GESTURE_MS
fields.type: { readonly press: 100; readonly release: 150; readonly tooltip: 100; readonly follow: 100; readonly leave: 100; readonly turn: 150; readonly slide: 150; readonly enter: 200; readonly list: 200; }
fields.doc: Durations in milliseconds of the gestures below; with `DURATION_MS`, all under 250 ms (test/animated.test.tsx).

fields.name: MOTION
fields.type: { readonly enter: { readonly duration: number; readonly ease: readonly [0, 0, 0, 1]; }; readonly list: { readonly duration: number; readonly ease: readonly [0.33, 0, 0.67, 1]; }; readonly leave: { re…
fields.doc: The transitions of the toolkit's motion, one per kind of movement: what enters decelerates, what leaves accelerates, what moves in place eases at both ends.

fields.name: TRAVEL_PX
fields.type: { readonly hint: 4; readonly card: 8; readonly row: 8; readonly notice: 24; readonly sheet: 32; }
fields.doc: How far a thing travels as it enters, in pixels on the 4px grid: the larger the surface, the longer the way, and always a small part of its own size (it settles into place, it does not cross the screen).

fields.name: NOTICES
fields.type: { readonly enter: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: 24; }; readonly close: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: 8; }; readonly pushed: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: number; }; readonly entering: …
fields.doc: The column of notices (`Toasts`): where a notice starts when it arrives and where it goes when it leaves. - `enter`: it rises from just below the column, fading in (`MOTION.enter`); - `close`: closed by the user or by its time, it sinks a little from where it stands and fades (`y` is added); - `pushed`: pushed out from the top by a newer notice, it goes up one more place and a little further, fading (`y` is added to that place). Both leave with `MOTION.leave`; - `transition`: the ones that stay move up one place or close the gap a notice left (`MOTION.list`). A notice keeps its size all the way: its text stays sharp and the column keeps its edge.

fields.name: LIST_ITEM
fields.type: { readonly initial: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly y: number; }; readonly animate: { readonly opacity: 1; readonly y: 0; }; readonly exit: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly transition: { readonly dura…
fields.doc: An item of an animated list (an app's list of entries, the new one on top): it comes down a few pixels into its place and fades in (`MOTION.enter`), while the others make room (`layout`, with `MOTION.list`). Leaving, it only fades, in the short time (`MOTION.leave`): it stands still and is gone before the others have closed up over its place.

fields.name: CARD_DURATION_MS
fields.doc: Duration of the entrance of the card of a menu or popover, in milliseconds (under 250).

fields.name: ROW_EXIT
fields.type: { readonly initial: false; readonly exit: { readonly opacity: 0; readonly height: 0; readonly paddingTop: 0; readonly paddingBottom: 0; readonly marginTop: 0; readonly marginBottom: 0; }; readonly tr…
fields.doc: A row (or a card) leaving the list, usually because it was completed: the row may have already dimmed on click (the app's row decides), here it fades and closes up in height, so the rows below rise without a jolt. No entrance: a new row appears still. The height is animated without `layout` (see above): the one motion outside transform and opacity. The row itself leaves (it fades accelerating, in the short time); the room it took closes up as a movement in place.

fields.name: PRESS_SCALE
fields.doc: A button goes down a little while pressed and comes back: 0.96 is about a pixel on each side of a 40px control, enough to be seen and too little to look like a bounce. Under the pointer it stays still by default (1), as desktop buttons do, in rows where many sit side by side. An app may ask for a hover scale.

files.about:
True for a press on the bar of a window (`TitleBar`). In a desktop frame the overlays open under the bar, so a
press on it is outside them: but the user is moving or minimizing the window, not leaving the dialog.

Where the overlays of a subtree mount (menus, popovers, selects, tooltips, dialogs, sheets): the page's body, or the
element a `PortalContainerProvider` names. Below the primitives: they read it, and it imports none of them.

components.name: PortalContainerProvider
components.doc: Where the overlays of this subtree mount: menus, popovers, selects, tooltips and dialogs. By default the page's `document.body`. An app that draws part of its React tree into another document (a popup window, an iframe) wraps that part with the other document's body, so its overlays open there and not in the page that owns the tree. `null` is the page's body: a provider whose element is not there yet (a layer that mounts with its children) keeps its place in the tree, so nothing under it is mounted twice when the element arrives.

files.about:
The colors of a user's labels (tags): eight background/ink pairs per scheme in `theme.css` (`--tag-1-*` …
`--tag-8-*`), picked from the label's name, so the same name has the same color everywhere and on every device,
without an extra datum. The chips of the labels field (`ChipsInput.tsx`) use them, and so can an app's own label pills.

Palettes from one base colour (owner, 2026-11-20: "selezionando un colore di base deve in automatico creare una
palette complementare + accento, e far scegliere solo tra 3 combinazioni"). Material Color Utilities finds the hues
that go with the colour (its complement by temperature, its tertiary); the theme engine then builds the theme from
them, so every contrast threshold holds as for the catalogue's themes. Two mood colours set the theme, the accent
makes it the user's.

types.name: PalettePick
types.doc: The user's palette: one base colour (`#rrggbb`) and how the rest follows from it.

files.about:
The shape of a theme definition, and the fonts. The toolkit ships no themes: each app passes its own definitions
and the engine (theme-engine.ts) derives every colour from them, guaranteeing the contrast
thresholds. Four things make a theme: the tint of the grays (`hue`) and how strong it is (`chroma`), the accent
(saturation and hue) and the sidebar: `tenue` (light, the tone of the app's ground), `scura` (a near-black, almost
neutral column in both schemes) or `piena` (in the theme's colour, with the selected item solid). Optional: a strong
`fill`, a `second` colour for the selection, or a curated palette's own `surfaces`.

fields.name: stack
fields.doc: The `font-family` stack: the font, then Inter (always in the app) and the system fallback.

fields.name: paper
fields.doc: The page.

fields.name: sidebar
fields.doc: The sidebar and the lanes, a step away from the page.

fields.name: raised
fields.doc: The raised sheets ("Now", panels, menus).

fields.name: line
fields.doc: The dividers.

fields.name: ink
fields.doc: The strongest text.

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent as text.

fields.name: fill
fields.doc: The filled button, "today", the bars.

types.name: ThemeDark
types.doc: The dark scheme of a theme, as parameters the engine computes the backgrounds from (`ThemeDef.dark`).

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: Absent: `DEFAULT_DARK_DEPTH`.

fields.name: tint
fields.doc: Absent: `DEFAULT_DARK_TINT`.

fields.name: hue
fields.doc: OKLCH hue of the grays (page, lines, ink).

fields.name: chroma
fields.doc: OKLCH chroma of the grays: almost zero, just a tint.

fields.name: accent
fields.doc: The accent: OKLCH saturation and hue. Zero saturation ("Ink"): the accent is the ink itself.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc: How round the corners are. Absent: `sharp` (2/4/6px). A value that is not a shape counts as absent.

fields.name: radii
fields.doc: The corner radii in px, for an app whose corners are none of the three shapes (for example 4/6/8/12): `sm`, `md`, `lg` and `xl` go to `--radius-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` and `-xl`; `button` and `chip` default to `md`. Absent, or not whole numbers (0 to 64; `button` and `chip` to 9999, a pill): the radii of `shape`.

fields.name: dark
fields.doc: The dark scheme: how deep it is and whether its backgrounds take the theme's hue. Absent, or with no valid value: the standard neutral anthracite. A curated palette (`surfaces`) keeps its own backgrounds, whatever is here.

fields.name: fill
fields.doc: A strong accent: the OKLCH lightness and chroma of the fill (the hue is the accent's). Without it the fill is the accent as text in light, and a deeper tone of it in dark. The engine still guarantees the label and the 3:1.

fields.name: second
fields.doc: A second color (OKLCH chroma and hue) for the selected item, when it is not the accent's: the page and the selection are one calm color, the filled button another that stands out ("teal to focus, orange to act").

fields.name: spot
fields.doc: The spot color (`#rrggbb`): a second, louder color for the few things that ask for attention now (what is due, what is running), never for structure. Without it the spot tokens are the theme's own fill and accent.

fields.name: surfaces
fields.type: { readonly light: Surfaces; readonly dark: Surfaces; }
fields.doc: A curated palette: the theme's own surfaces, ink and accents in each scheme, as `#rrggbb`, instead of the common lightness ladder. The engine still corrects text, accents and borders until they hold the contrast thresholds.

types.name: ThemeRadii
types.doc: The corner radii of a theme in px (`ThemeDef.radii`).

files.about:
The theme engine: a theme definition (its shape is in theme-catalog.ts; the app brings its own themes), in light or in
dark, gives the values of all the `--color-*` tokens and of the shape variables. The starting lightness values are those of the approved sketch
(design/bozzetti/lista-attivita.html, `coloriDi`), the same for every theme: that is why every theme reads the same. The colors
are computed in OKLCH, brought back to sRGB by reducing chroma, and the contrast is guaranteed in the computation, on the final
hex values: a color below the threshold is darkened on light backgrounds and lightened on dark ones until
it gets there. Fixed, never from the theme: the destructive red and the status colours.
The solid button (`primary`) is the accent as a fill: in light it coincides with the accent as text, in dark it is a

The words of the toolkit. A component's content is the app's: what a field holds, what a button says, the title
of a dialog all come from the caller. What is left here are the few words a component has to say by itself: the

take the words as their last argument: `useWords()` gives them to an app's own component.

Sigrid's icons (R6 of the toolkit's rules): icons are visual anchors for the eye, and Sigrid has one set of its own,
Lucide (the owner, 2026-11-23: «Sigrid deve avere un suo unico icon set»), the same in every app. A component asks
for an icon by what it means (`settings`, `delete`), never by Lucide's own name, so a meaning keeps its drawing in
every app. An icon a function needs that is not among the names is added here, to Sigrid's names, never by an app.
That binds every app: an app imports no icon. The toolkit's own parts take `Icon` too wherever a name has the
meaning; a part draws a Lucide glyph directly only where `Icon` cannot give the same thing: a glyph no name means
(the sort arrows of a table, the grip of a row moved by hand, the dot of a radio item, the fit of the graph, the kinds
of an item, which `kindIcon` hands out as Lucide's components), or a glyph that holds what `Icon`'s wrapping `<span>`
would take from it (its own place, `ml-auto` or `absolute`: the submenu's chevron, the search field's magnifier; the
bar's drag attribute; a `data-slot`; its place in a box that is not a flex box, where the wrapper moves it by a pixel:
the chevron of a select, the check of a ring, a menu or a list), or a stroke `Icon` does not take (the heavier check
on a card of the look settings).
The other packs (Phosphor Duotone, Solar Duotone, Fluent Color, Fluent Emoji Flat, Twemoji), the user's choice of a
pack and an app's own icons left on 2026-11-23.

components.name: Icon
components.doc: An icon by its meaning, drawn from Sigrid's set. Decorative: the label next to it names the thing, so it is hidden from screen readers. A name Sigrid does not draw (from data) is an empty slot of the same size, so the row keeps its alignment (R6).

@acaprino/sigrid/primitives, the first level: one control or one surface each, with no idea of what it holds. A
button, a field, a check, a menu, a sheet, a hint, an icon, and the parts a screen is laid out with (`Column`,
`Cluster`, `Text`…). Ark UI and Base UI give the behaviour, Park UI's recipes the form. A primitive imports no
component, no part of the frame and no assembly (test/layers.test.ts).

From Park's `avatar` recipe comes the form (its subtle variant, its full shape): a round tile with the picture
cropped to fill it, or the initials in medium weight when there is no picture. Ours: three sizes on the toolkit's
control heights (36, 32 and 28px at normal density; Park's go from 24 to 64px), 12px initials below the largest, and a
neutral fill for every person: the quiet gray of the label pills, with the ink. A person's colour is not a fill
(R10: data colours are dots); an app that gives people a colour puts a dot beside the name.
Behaviour: Ark UI's Avatar, which shows the initials until the picture has loaded and again if it fails.
The name is the avatar's accessible name, unless `decorative` says the name is written beside it.

The initials take the ink with the better contrast on it (white or black). Without it the tile is the neutral one (R10: a colour for a person is a dot, not a fill): this is for what the app chose on purpose.

From SmoothButton we keep: the plain `<button>` with `type="button"` by default and `asChild` without Radix's Slot
(here with Base UI's `useRender`, which merges classes, styles, handlers and ref like the Slot). Our variant and size
names stay (the ones the package uses).
From Park's `button` recipe comes the form: l2 corners, and its variants and sizes under our names. The label is
medium (Park's is semibold: lighter here).
Variants: `default` is Park's solid, `secondary` its subtle in the neutral gray, `outline` its outline (with the 3:1
control border), `ghost` its plain, `destructive` its subtle in red; `link` is ours. A neutral subtle chip is
`QUIET_CHIP` below, for an app's chips: it is not a public variant.
Sizes: `default`, `sm` and `xs` are 36, 32 and 28px at normal density, one 4px step under Park's md, sm and xs (40, 36
and 32px, which is the large density); `lg` is the default height with a 16px label; the `icon-*` sizes are the same
heights, square. Colors are the theme engine's
tokens, not Park's palettes. Focus: the toolkit's ring (`lib/focus.ts`, R8).
The variant `secondary` is Park's subtle in the neutral gray (R4: no border and shadow together).
Motion, only with `animated` true and without prefers-reduced-motion: the button goes down a little while pressed
(`tapScale`) and, if asked, grows under the pointer (`hoverScale`). The gestures are attached to the `<button>` that is
already there (`pressable` in `motion-impl`), so the element is the same with animations on or off and nothing
remounts when the Motion chunk arrives. With `animated` false the DOM is the same as before.
Park's `loading` state, without its spinner (the owner's decision of 2026-11-20: no looping animation, as the
attachment viewer): a busy button keeps its size and its place, is `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` (it keeps focus,
unlike `disabled`), ignores clicks and the pointer, and may show the caller's `loadingText` ("Saving…") in place of
its label. With `loadingText` the label and the loading text share one grid cell (`SwapLabel`), so the width is the
wider of the two before, during and after the wait.

A surface that holds a group of content that stands apart from the page: the one thing to do now, the item being
sorted, a card of a board, a summary beside a message. Two forms (R4): `raised`, the raised surface with the smallest
shadow and no border (a card that can be picked up, a board's card); `quiet`, the quiet fill of the page with no
shadow (a lane, a group of rows, a note set apart). The large corner, as every surface that holds controls.
Not every group is a card («Lines and space, not boxes», docs/design-laws.md): a group is told first by the space
around it (`Column`, `Section`), then by a line; a card is for the few groups that are a thing of their own.
Its inside is a pile (`Column`'s steps): what is in it is laid out with no class of the app's own, and a class or a
style passed in spite of the types never reaches the page.

The layout of a screen with no class of the app's own: a pile, a wrapping row, two groups at the two ends of a row, an
automatic grid, a spacer, a named section, an area that scrolls, the body of a page (or a page of exactly one screen,
`Page fit`), and the weight of a line of text.
Every space is a step of the scale (`Space`: xs 4, sm 8, md 12, lg 16, xl 24px). No part takes a class or a style, and
one passed in spite of the types is dropped: an app that lays out a screen with these writes no class (the owner's
rule of 2026-11-23: an app has no interface code of its own).
After Imago's helpers (`im-stack`, `im-cluster`, `im-split`, `im-auto-grid`, `im-spacer`, `im-section`, `im-scroll`,
`im-page-content`, `im-muted`, `im-caption`, `im-kicker`, `im-readout`). The pile is `Column`: «Stack» names a view
of an app, which the toolkit does not carry (test/build.test.ts).
`Column fill` is a pile as tall as the region that holds it, so that one of its parts (a `GraphCanvas fill`, a
`VirtualList fill`, an `Empty fill`) takes the height the others leave, with no class of the app's. With a canvas in
it, it is never shorter than what its parts need, so the canvas at its floor covers nothing that follows the pile.
`Column width` keeps a pile to the width of a column of text or of content, centred; `Cluster wrap={false}` keeps a
row on one line (an avatar and its words); `Text` also has the soft ink of running text, the strong words of a line
and the 13px note beside a title.

How far a task is: a bar (`Progress`), a ring (`ProgressRing`) or blocks (`ProgressSegments`), one API for the three.
Written by hand: Ark's Progress names the bar with its own value («45%») and gives no `aria-valuetext`, and there is no
keyboard to inherit; here the app names the bar, the toolkit says the value. The form is Park UI's progress recipe
(102769c): a track 8px (`sm`) or 10px (`md`) tall with the corners of a control (l1), the range filling it from the
start. Not taken from it: the stripes, the gradient of its indeterminate state and its animation (no gradient, no
loop but the skeletons: DESIGN.md), and the pill shape (round only for avatars, dots and switches, R7).
The ring and the blocks are ours; Park's circular recipe was not read.
The colours: the track is the quiet fill (the ink at 6%), the range is the accent as progress (R2); done is the
success colour and a failure the destructive one, each with a word (DESIGN.md "Status": a colour is never alone).
A failure also has the one look it has everywhere: Sigrid's `error` icon (the circle with an X), inside the ring and
before the word of the bar and of the blocks.
Nothing moves: the range jumps to the value, as the steps do. A progress that changes by events (an upload) is not a
gesture, so no tween (DESIGN.md Motion). The range is `primary`, the fill of the accent, as in the checkbox and the
switch (DESIGN.md Colors).
Not knowing how far it is (`value={null}`) is a track with no range and the word «In progress», not a loop.
In a line of words (the frame's status row, docs/patterns.md «Progress of a task») the bar is `inline`: a fixed width
that does not give way, so the words beside it stay put while the value moves.
For screen readers: `role="progressbar"` named by the app, with `aria-valuenow` and, always, `aria-valuetext` («45%»,
«Complete»). The visible text repeats it and is hidden from them. A page that updates a value often should
announce the end and the failure only, in a live region of its own, not every percent.

Park UI (MIT) drawer 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/drawer.ts)
From Park's `drawer` recipe comes the elevation (lg, in place of a border: no border on the inner edge, R4) and the
backdrop (the `drop` color, at the 40% of `BACKDROP`, the same as the dialog's). The title is 16px semibold (Park's is 20px: R7, text sizes from the toolkit's tokens).
From SmoothUI's Drawer we keep Base UI's primitives (Root, Portal, Backdrop, Viewport, Popup, Content), the
drag direction per side and the content marked `Drawer.Content` (a mouse drag that starts
there does not move the sheet: the text of the fields can be selected). Removed: the 400 ms CSS transitions, the spring and the
staggering of the children with Motion, the handle of the bottom side. The entrance (32 px from the panel edge, 200 ms) follows
the shared Motion preference and respects reduced motion.

components.name: Sheet
components.doc: A modal sheet: focus trapped, Esc and a click outside close it, page scrolling is blocked. With `modal={false}` it is a side panel beside the page: no backdrop, the focus is not trapped, the page scrolls and takes clicks, and Esc or a click outside still close it (`disablePointerDismissal` keeps it open on a click outside). A click on the notifications (which sit above, outside the sheet) does not close it: Base UI closes a modal only on what is behind it, and here a second safeguard also cancels the closing caused by focus moving to the notifications.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.doc: `reason` is told when it closes: an app that keeps a form in the sheet may answer a press outside differently from the Esc.

props.name: closesOnEscape
props.doc: Asked at each Esc: false leaves the sheet open and the key to what has the focus and to the app's commands (the `Inspector` beside the page answers it so, when the focus is not in it). Absent: Esc always closes the sheet.

props.name: width
props.doc: At the side (`left`, `right`): the widest it grows, `sm` 384px (the default), `md` 448px, `lg` 512px. Ignored at the top or the foot.

props.name: onCloseAutoFocus
props.doc: On closing, before the focus moves (like Radix's `onCloseAutoFocus`): `event.preventDefault()` says that the caller has already taken care of the focus, and the sheet no longer touches it.

props.name: animated
props.doc: Animate the entrance from the configured edge. Inherits the provider preference.

Park UI (MIT) slider 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/slider.ts)
From Park's `slider` recipe comes the form (its md size, its outline variant): a round 8px track, the part up to the
value filled, and a round 20px thumb with a 2px border, centred on the track. Ours: the track is the `input` token
(3:1 on every background, WCAG 1.4.11; Park's is its hairline border colour), the filled part and the thumb's
border are the ink (the accent is kept for the primary action, R2), the thumb is the paper with no shadow (R4: a
bordered control has no shadow). The thumb's area is 44px with a coarse pointer.
Behaviour: Ark UI's Slider, one thumb (`role="slider"`): Left and Right move by `step`, PageUp and PageDown by ten
steps, Home and End go to the ends; Up and Down act as Right and Left, as the ARIA pattern has it. No animation: the
thumb follows the pointer.

props.name: onValueChange
props.doc: Called with each value while the thumb moves.

props.name: step
props.doc: The distance between two values. Default 1.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: The name of the slider for screen readers.

Park UI (MIT) switch 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/switch.ts)
From Park's `switch` recipe comes the form (its md size, its solid variant): a round 40x20px track and a round thumb
of 16px (Park's 20px thumb at scale 0.8), 2px from the edge, that sits at the start when off and at the end when on.
Ours: the track at rest is the `input` token (3:1 on every background, WCAG 1.4.11; Park's is its subtle gray) and
the track when on is the ink, as the checkbox's fill: the accent is kept for the primary action (R2). The thumb is
the paper in both states. No shadow on the thumb (R4: the track is a fill, the thumb a flat dot). The hit area grows
with a pseudo-element, as the checkbox's: 28px on every pointer, 44px on a coarse one.
Behaviour: Ark UI's Switch (a hidden checkbox with `role="switch"` inside a `<label>`; Space toggles). Without
`animated` the thumb changes place at once; with it (or under a `MotionProvider`) it slides in 100 ms, never with
`prefers-reduced-motion`.

props.name: checked
props.doc: On (controlled).

props.name: defaultChecked
props.doc: Initial state when uncontrolled.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.doc: Called with the new state when the user turns it on or off.

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the control itself, for a `<label htmlFor>` elsewhere.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: The name for screen readers when there is no visible label.

props.name: children
props.doc: The visible label, after the control: a click on it toggles too.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The thumb slides to its new place (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

files.about:
A table: rows of the same things, each with the same facts in columns. These are the parts of its form and nothing
more: a `<table>` in a box that scrolls, a heading row, rows and cells, drawn with the toolkit's tokens so every
table of an app reads as the others do.
- A row is as tall as the density's row (44px with a finger), with a line under it and no other frame (R4).
- A heading is small muted text (the label size); a column of numbers is set at the end, in tabular figures (R5).
- The row chosen has the selection tint, stronger text and a short accent bar at its start (R1), as in every list;
  under the pointer a row takes a share of that tint.
What a table does (sorting, filtering, choosing columns, drawing only the rows in sight) is not here: `DataTable`
(the `./table` entry of the package) does the first and the last on TanStack Table, and an app with a table of its
own drives it with the library it likes and draws it with these parts.

props.name: containerClassName
props.doc: The classes of the box around the table, which scrolls: its height, where the rows are many.

props.name: containerRef
props.doc: The box around the table, for what has to read its scrolling.

components.name: TableCaption
components.doc: The name of the table, for everyone: above it, small and muted. A table can be named with `aria-label` instead.

props.name: align
props.doc: `end`: a number, in tabular figures.

props.name: align
props.doc: `end`: over a column of numbers.

props.name: sticky
props.doc: The heading stays in sight while the rows scroll under it.

props.name: current
props.doc: This row is the one chosen: the selection tint, stronger text and the accent bar. One for each table (R1).

Park UI (MIT) tabs 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/tabs.ts)
From Park's `tabs` recipe comes the form (its md size, its subtle variant): a row of triggers 40px tall with 14px
semibold text, 16px of side padding and a 4px gap between them, the chosen one on a tinted sheet with l2 corners,
and the panels below, 8px away. The tint is the theme's selection (`selected`, with `selected-ink`), the one tint a
view has for what is chosen (R1); the others are muted text that turns to ink under the pointer. Park's `line`
variant (a 2px bar under the chosen tab) is not offered: R1 keeps bars off the toolkit. For a choice with no panels
use `ToggleGroup` (Park's `enclosed` look).
Behaviour: Ark UI's Tabs (`role="tablist"`, one Tab stop, arrows move and, by default, choose; Home and End). With
`animated` the tint is one sheet that slides from the old tab to the new one (`Highlight` in `motion-impl`).

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen tab.

props.name: activation
props.doc: `automatic` (the default): the arrows choose as they move. `manual`: they only move, Enter or Space chooses.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The tint slides to the new tab (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

props.name: ids
props.type: { trigger?: ((value: string) => string) | undefined; content?: ((value: string) => string) | undefined; }
props.doc: The ids of the tabs and of their panels by value, for an app that draws the panels itself and names them (`aria-labelledby`). They go to Ark, which finds the tabs by them for the arrows: an `id` set on a tab afterwards would lose the arrows.

components.name: TabsContent
components.doc: The panel of a tab: in the page only while its tab is chosen, and a Tab stop of its own, after the tabs.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the group of tabs for screen readers.

props.name: end
props.doc: After the tab, in the same item: a button that acts on it (closing it). It is not a tab: it keeps its own Tab stop, and the arrows still move from tab to tab. With it the tab and the button sit in one `data-slot="tabs-item"` element.

props.name: itemClassName
props.doc: The class of that item (only with `end`).

components.name: Textarea
components.doc: A multi-line field. Same API as before: the props of `<textarea>` (`ref` reaches the `<textarea>`). Base UI's types describe an `<input>`: with `render` the element is a `<textarea>`, so the props are passed with a cast.

The only sources a thumbnail accepts: a JPEG or PNG image in base64, whole in the string. No `javascript:`,
`data:text/html`, `data:image/svg+xml` (it can carry script), `http:` or `blob:`: the thumbnail comes from the app as
a data URL and no other value must ever reach `src`.

components.name: NeedThumbnail
components.doc: Asks for a thumbnail only once per mounted row: when `when` becomes true it calls `onNeed(id)`, then never again for that id, even if the value stays null (no loop). It draws nothing.

components.name: Thumbnail
components.doc: A square thumbnail (`object-fit: cover`) or, until there is one, a neutral box of the same size. Still.

props.name: src
props.doc: The data URL; null, absent or not acceptable: the neutral box with the mark of the kind.

props.name: kind
props.doc: The mark of the neutral box.

props.name: size
props.doc: 64px in the details, 40px on the rows.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name for assistive technology (the kind: «file»), or null if the row already says it or it is not needed. The image always has an empty `alt`: the title next to it already says what it is.

props.name: onOpen
props.doc: A click on the thumbnail does what «Open» does. It is a button (never a link), out of the Tab order and hidden from assistive technology: for keyboard and screen readers there is already «Open» in the same row, and two buttons with the same name would be a duplicate.

SmoothUI (MIT) toggle-group 4.0.0 — adapted for @acaprino/sigrid (https://smoothui.dev/r/base-nova/toggle-group.json)
Park UI (MIT) segment-group 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/segment-group.ts)
From Park's `segment-group` recipe comes the form (its md size): a quiet gray group with l3 corners and a hairline
ring inside its edge, no padding, items 40px tall with 14px medium text and 14px of side padding, and the chosen item
as a raised sheet with l3 corners (Park's indicator, here with its xs elevation, as in the approved preview).
With `animated` the background of the pressed item is one pill that slides from the old choice to the new one
(`Highlight` in `motion-impl`, `MOTION.slide`). The group only chooses: it shows no panels.
From SmoothUI we keep the primitive (Base UI's `ToggleGroup` and `Toggle`) and the shape of the segmented control
(container with a light background, pressed item raised). Adapted: single choice only (the already pressed button
does not turn off: the group always has a value), paper/ink tokens in place of `foreground`/`muted`, no
shadow or dark variant, and the toolkit's focus ring (`lib/focus.ts`, R8, like the other controls). SmoothUI's `Toggle`
button (slug `toggle`) is not copied: the item uses Base UI's `Toggle` directly. Base UI gives
`role="group"`, `aria-pressed` on the buttons and a single tab stop with the arrows (which restart from the beginning).
The group is as wide as its items, wherever it is put (in a pile that stretches its parts, too); with `fill` it is as
wide as its place and its items share it equally, as two halves of a switch on a phone, so neither grows when pressed.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.doc: Single-choice group: a single tab stop, arrows to move, Space/Enter to choose.

props.name: value
props.doc: The pressed value.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Name of the group for screen readers.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The background of the pressed item slides to the new choice (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

props.name: fill
props.doc: As wide as its place, the items sharing it equally (a switch across a phone). Absent: as wide as its items.

props.name: highlightClassName
props.doc: With animations on: the classes of the sliding pill (background, corners), in place of the pressed item's own background.

SmoothUI (MIT) tooltip 4.0.0 — adapted for @acaprino/sigrid (https://smoothui.dev/r/base-nova/tooltip.json)
Park UI (MIT) tooltip 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/tooltip.ts)
From Park's `tooltip` recipe comes the form: a solid ink card with l2 corners, the sm elevation, 12px semibold text,
8px by 6px of padding.
From SmoothUI we keep the primitive (Base UI's `Tooltip`: Root, Trigger with `render`, Portal, Positioner, Popup) and the
shape of the card (ink on paper, small text). Adapted to icon-only buttons: the text is the button's accessible
name (`label`, the same as its `aria-label`), not free content; no Provider (each
hint has its own delay, 500 ms), no controlled state. Removed: SmoothUI's CSS transitions
(the opacity and transform transition with the entrance scale): with `animated` true (off by default, never with
prefers-reduced-motion) the card fades in a few pixels from its button in 100 ms (`enterTooltip` in `motion-impl`).
Base UI places and labels it.
The hint does not capture the pointer (`pointer-events-none`, `disableHoverablePopup`), closes on click on the
button and with Esc, and sits below sheets and windows (`z-[45]`: above the drawer, z-40, below the sheets, z-50). The accessible
name stays only the `aria-label`: the card is `aria-hidden` (Base UI does not add `aria-describedby`), so a
screen reader does not hear it twice.

components.name: Tooltip
components.doc: The hint of an icon-only button: it repeats its name on pointer hover and on focus. The button stays the same as before (same `aria-label`, same Tab), without `title`.

props.name: label
props.doc: The hint text: the button's accessible name, in English.

props.name: shortcut
props.doc: The key that does the same («Ctrl K»): plain text after the name, never a boxed key (R5).

props.name: children
props.doc: The button (a single element): it receives the hint's handlers via Base UI's `render`, without an extra node.

props.name: side
props.doc: Where it sits, if there is room. Default below.

props.name: sideOffset
props.doc: Distance from the button in px.

props.name: delay
props.doc: Hover delay in ms. Default 500.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The card fades in quickly (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

Park UI (MIT) date-picker 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/date-picker.ts)

From Park's `date-picker` recipe (and its component, which draws each day as a plain icon button) comes the look: the
title between two plain arrows, the weekday row in semibold muted text, the days as 36px plain buttons (Park's sm)
with l2 corners and a quiet fill under the pointer, the chosen day solid in the accent (Park's solid variant), today
marked by a short accent dash under the number, 16px of padding. The grid itself is not written here: it is the day,
month and year views of Ark UI's DatePicker (`@ark-ui/react/date-picker`). It lives inside a `DatePicker.Root` (see
`components/DateField.tsx`), which holds the value.
Ark gives the grid and its keyboard (arrows between days, PageUp and PageDown for the month, with Shift for the year,
Home and End for the week, Enter chooses; one day only has `tabIndex` 0), the days outside the month, today, the
title that opens the months and then the years, and the announcement of the month when it changes.
Ours: the sizes (`--cell-size` is the density token `--control-sm`, 2.25rem at `normal`, 2.75rem with a finger; the days outside the month softer), the names in English (see `CALENDAR_WORDS`), a real `<button>` for each day (Space
chooses too), the weekday headers left readable by screen readers, with the full name in `abbr`, and Home and End
for the start and the end of the week, as in the APG date grid (Ark's go to the start and the end of the month).

props.name: onPressSelected
props.doc: A click, Enter or Space on the day that is already chosen calls this instead of choosing it again (the reminder uses it to remove the day).

Park UI (MIT) tags-input 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/tags-input.ts)

From Park's `tags-input` recipe (md) comes the look: the field 40px tall with l2 corners and 6px of side padding,
6px between the chips, each chip 28px tall with l1 corners and its own 20px remove button. What the field does rests
on Ark UI's TagsInput (`@ark-ui/react/tags-input`).
Ark gives: Enter and the comma that close a label, a pasted «a, b, c» split into labels, the text left in the box
added when the field is left, the arrows that walk the chips from the box (Delete or Backspace removes the one
reached), the remove button of each chip with its name, the announcements to screen readers, one Tab stop for the
whole field. Ours: the chip is the neutral `Badge` with a dot in the color of its name (`tag-color.ts`, R10); the words are about
«labels», in English; a label already there is not added again whatever its case; Backspace in the empty box removes
the last label at once (Ark would first select it and remove it at the second press); a chip is not edited in place;
a comma that arrives with other text in one go (an autocorrection, a keyboard's suggestion) closes the labels before
it and leaves the rest in the box (Ark would add the text it had before that event).
With `suggestions` the box is also a combobox (Ark UI's Combobox, on the same text box): while the user writes, the
labels that match and are not in the field yet are listed under it; the arrows move, Enter or a click adds the one
reached, Esc closes the list only. Any other text is still a label of its own (Enter, the comma, leaving the box).
No animation.

components.name: ChipsInput
components.doc: A list of labels as chips with an input: add with Enter or comma (also by pasting «a, b, c» or by leaving the input), remove with the chip's button, and with Backspace on an empty input the last one is removed.

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the writing input, for the field's label.

props.name: suggestions
props.doc: Labels to offer while the user writes (the ones used elsewhere, people from an address book). The ones already in the field are left out. Filtered here by the text typed, ignoring case, unless `onQuery` is given.

props.name: onQuery
props.doc: The text being typed: with it the caller filters (and may fetch) and passes the new `suggestions`.

props.name: suggestionsLabel
props.doc: The name of the list of suggestions for screen readers. Absent: the toolkit's words («Suggestions»).

props.name: display
props.doc: What a chip shows in place of its value (a person's name in place of the whole address). The value stays what the caller holds and what a chip is told apart by; a suggestion shows the name and, after it, the value in the muted ink, and is found by either.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: True for a value that is not valid (an address without its domain): its chip has the destructive border and text, and screen readers hear so after its name. The field does not refuse it: the caller decides what to do with it.

props.name: separators
props.doc: The characters that close a label, each one a single character. Default: the comma. Enter always closes one. A separator typed, pasted or arriving with other text splits it the same way (`[',', ';', ' ']` for addresses).

props.name: dot
props.doc: The 8px dot in the colour of the label's name (R10), on by default. Off for chips that are not coloured labels (people, addresses).

Park UI (MIT) combobox 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/combobox.ts)
From Park's `combobox` recipe comes the form (its md size, its outline variant): the field is the toolkit's input
(40px, l2 corners, the 3:1 border) with the chevron at its end, and the list is the select's (l2 corners, the md
elevation, 4px of padding, a 2px gap, rows at least 40px tall with 8px of side padding and l1 corners). The row
under the pointer or the arrows is the quiet fill; the chosen one carries a check, in the ink (Park's is its accent).
Behaviour: Ark UI's Combobox: typing filters, the arrows move, Enter chooses, Esc closes the list first. The text
must end as one of the options: on leaving, a text that is none goes back to the chosen one.
Ours: the options are filtered here by their label, ignoring case, unless the caller answers `onQuery` with a new
list (people from a server); the list is not moved to a portal (as the date field's card: it stays inside the sheet
that holds it, and `fixed` keeps a scrolling body from clipping it). No animation.

props.name: value
props.doc: The chosen value, or null.

props.name: onQuery
props.doc: The text being typed: with it the caller filters (and may fetch) and passes the new `options`; the list here is then shown as given. Without it the options are filtered by their label.

props.name: id
props.doc: The id of the text box, for the field's `<label>`.

props.name: emptyText
props.doc: What the list says when nothing matches. Absent: the toolkit's words («No results»).

props.name: triggerLabel
props.doc: The name of the button that opens the list. Absent: the toolkit's words («Show the options»).

fields.name: detail
fields.doc: A second line of muted text (a person's address under the name).

A button that puts a text on the clipboard and says that it did. After the press the copy icon is a check and the
word is «Copied» for two seconds, then both go back: the answer is where the eye already is, so no notice is needed
(a toast is for an action that can be taken back). Nothing moves: the icon keeps its box and the word the room of
the wider of its two texts. Screen readers hear «Copied» (a polite status), or that the system refused.
Alone it is a quiet icon button with a hint; with `showLabel` it shows its word; in an `InputGroup` it takes the
size of the group's buttons and is off with the field.

props.name: animated
props.doc: The button goes down a little while pressed (off by default, never with prefers-reduced-motion).

props.name: hoverScale
props.doc: Scale under the pointer, with `animated`. Default 1: still.

props.name: tapScale
props.doc: Override the default press scale (0.96 with at most 2px of travel per edge).

props.name: value
props.doc: The text put on the clipboard.

props.name: label
props.doc: The name of the action («Copy the link»): the accessible name, the hint, and the word with `showLabel`. Absent: the toolkit's word («Copy»).

props.name: showLabel
props.doc: The word beside the icon. Without it the button shows the icon alone.

props.name: onCopied
props.doc: Called once the text is on the clipboard.

props.name: onCopyError
props.doc: Called when the system refused the clipboard.

Park UI (MIT) input 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/input.ts)
From Park's `input` recipe (md): the button that opens the calendar has the field's form (40px, l2 corners, 12px of
side padding); the card is Park's date-picker content (l3 corners, the lg elevation).
The date field: a button that shows the date and opens the calendar, on Ark UI's DatePicker
(`@ark-ui/react/date-picker`). Two variants (a form can use both), with the same contract as the native fields they
replace: `DateField` gives and receives `YYYY-MM-DD` (or null), `DateTimeField` `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm` in local time
(or null; the time is switched on with the «Time» checkbox, otherwise 09:00). Only formatting of local dates: no time
zones, no «tomorrow». The button takes the `id` of the field's `<label>` (accessible name «Due date», «Reminder»).
Ark gives: the open state and its dismissal (Esc or a click outside close without choosing, and focus returns to the
button), the position of the card, focus on the chosen day when it opens, the grid (see `ui/calendar.tsx`).
The card is not moved to a portal: it stays inside the field, so it is part of the modal sheet that holds it (its
focus trap, its Esc), and `fixed` keeps the scrolling body of the sheet from clipping it.

components.name: DateField
components.doc: A local date (a due date, a birthday): a click or Enter on a day chooses it and closes.

props.name: value
props.doc: `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty/null.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The button text without a value. Absent: the toolkit's words («No date», «No date and time»).

props.name: min
props.doc: The first and the last day that can be chosen, as `YYYY-MM-DD`: the days outside are not chosen.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The field cannot be opened: half opacity, out of the Tab order.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale of the date on the button and of the month and weekday names (a BCP 47 tag). Default `en-US`.

props.name: words
props.type: { time?: string | undefined; timeOfDay?: string | undefined; done?: string | undefined; }
props.doc: The words of the reminder's foot, for this field only: otherwise the toolkit's words (`WordsProvider`).

props.name: picks
props.doc: Quick choices in a row above the calendar: `dayPicks()` gives today, tomorrow and this weekend.

components.name: DateRangeField
components.doc: A range of local days (a stay, a leave, a filter): a click chooses the first day, a second one the last and closes; the days between take the selection tint. The two clicks may come in either order, and on the same day for a range of one day. The caller hears of a range only when it has both ends.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The field cannot be opened: half opacity, out of the Tab order.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The button text without a value. Absent: the toolkit's words («No date», «No date and time»).

props.name: min
props.doc: The first and the last day that can be chosen, as `YYYY-MM-DD`: the days outside are not chosen.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale of the date on the button and of the month and weekday names (a BCP 47 tag). Default `en-US`.

props.name: value
props.doc: The two ends as `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null. A value whose ends are not real dates, or are the wrong way round, reads as null.

props.name: picks
props.doc: Quick choices in a row above the calendar: `rangePicks()` gives this weekend and the next seven days.

components.name: DateTimeField
components.doc: A local day and, if needed, a local time (the reminder). Without a date there is no reminder. A click on a day chooses it and immediately gives `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm`; a click on the day already chosen removes it (no «Clear the date» button). The time is off by default: the «Time» checkbox turns it on, and when off it is 09:00. With a date already set the checkbox starts on if the time is not the default one. A half-typed time (the empty field while writing) never enters the value: the last valid one stays. «Done» or Esc closes.

props.name: value
props.doc: `YYYY-MM-DD` or empty/null.

props.name: placeholder
props.doc: The button text without a value. Absent: the toolkit's words («No date», «No date and time»).

props.name: min
props.doc: The first and the last day that can be chosen, as `YYYY-MM-DD`: the days outside are not chosen.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: The field cannot be opened: half opacity, out of the Tab order.

props.name: locale
props.doc: The locale of the date on the button and of the month and weekday names (a BCP 47 tag). Default `en-US`.

props.name: words
props.type: { time?: string | undefined; timeOfDay?: string | undefined; done?: string | undefined; }
props.doc: The words of the reminder's foot, for this field only: otherwise the toolkit's words (`WordsProvider`).

props.name: picks
props.doc: Quick choices in a row above the calendar: `dayPicks()` gives today, tomorrow and this weekend.

types.name: DatePick
types.doc: A quick choice of a date field: its name and the day it sets, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

types.name: DateRange
types.doc: A range of local days, both ends included: `start` is never after `end`.

types.name: DateRangePick
types.doc: A quick choice of a range field: its name and the two ends it sets, as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

The facts of one thing as names and values, in two columns: the names in the muted ink at the start, the values in
the ink beside them, one fact a line (the details of an item in an inspector: its name, its level, its path). It is a
`<dl>`, so a screen reader reads each name with its value. A value that is code, a path or an id is set in the
monospace face and broken anywhere, so a long one wraps in a narrow inspector instead of widening it.

components.name: DescriptionList
components.doc: Names and values, side by side: the facts of one thing.

props.name: items
props.doc: The facts, in the order they are read. A fact may be left out with `null` or `false`.

props.name: aria-label
props.doc: Its name for screen readers, where the heading above it does not name it.

types.name: DescriptionItem
types.doc: One fact: its name and its value.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: What the fact is («Level»).

fields.name: value
fields.doc: What it is worth («Recommended»).

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The value is code, a path or an id: the monospace face, broken anywhere.

components.name: Dialog
components.doc: Modal window on a raised surface: a name to change, a profile, confirmations.

props.name: title
props.doc: Accessible title of the window.

props.name: footer
props.doc: Actions at the bottom (usually a primary `Button` and a `ghost` one).

props.name: restoreFocusTo
props.doc: Where focus goes when it closes: the window opens from state, not from a `Trigger` that would get focus back, and without this focus ends up on the `body`. `restoreFocusTo` is the element that opened it; `onCloseAutoFocus` speaks first and can decide for itself (`event.preventDefault()`, then move focus wherever it wants). Both are optional.

props.name: drawer
props.doc: The form opens in a side panel on the right, like a details sheet. Without it, it is a window in the center of the page: the short confirmations.

files.about:
One row that opens in place: what most people do not need on most visits stays behind it, and the first view holds
the rest (progressive disclosure). The row is named for what it holds («Add a coupon»; «More options» only for a
mix). What is inside stays in the page while closed, so what was written there is kept, and the page does not move
the reader anywhere: it grows under the row. Base UI's `Collapsible` gives the behaviour (a button with
`aria-expanded` that names its panel); the form is the toolkit's: a quiet row with the chevron in the icon slot,
44px with a finger. Never inside another `Disclosure` that is itself inside one: two levels at most.
Never put behind it what people need before they commit: a price, a required field, what a delete removes.

props.name: label
props.doc: What the row holds, in the words people would look for («Add a coupon», «Advanced»).

props.name: summary
props.doc: A fact about what is inside, at the end of the row while it tells something («3 set», «Off»).

props.name: defaultOpen
props.doc: Open at first, for a row that keeps its own state. Default closed.

props.name: open
props.doc: Open or closed, when the app keeps it.

props.name: children
props.doc: What opens under the row.

A duration field: hours and minutes in two number inputs, four shortcuts and
«None». The field does not add, convert or check the total: it sends hours and minutes as they are and the app decides
(up to 24 hours, minutes from 0 to 59; zero and zero means «None»). Two inputs have no syntax to get wrong, and the
shortcuts cover the frequent cases with one click.

SmoothUI (MIT) empty 4.0.0 — adapted for @acaprino/sigrid (https://smoothui.dev/r/base-nova/empty.json) From SmoothUI we keep the structure (container, optional icon, title, sentence, action) and the `data-slot`s (`empty`, `empty-icon`, `empty-title`, `empty-description`, `empty-action`). With `fill` it is the whole of a view that has nothing to show: as tall as its region (in a `Column fill`, as what its other parts leave), centred in it, with a page's margins, so an app writes no class for it. Adapted: words only, no illustration by default (the icon stays optional and nobody passes it); `theme.css` tokens (`text-ink`, `text-ink-soft`, `bg-paper-2`) instead of `foreground`/`muted-foreground`; the title is a `
` and not an `

`), which would not be valid inside an `

` or a `

`. One need, one look: it says that there is nothing here. Something that failed (a view that could not load) is a `Note` with `tone="error"`, with «Retry» when it can be tried again. Spacing and size are chosen by whoever uses it with `className`/`titleClassName` (tailwind-merge). The title is 16px (the toolkit's title size, R7); the optional icon is a plain 16px muted icon, not a tile (R6, R7). No animation.

components.name: Empty
components.doc: The empty state of a view or a list («nothing here»): a title, a sentence if needed and an action. Also the end of a task of several steps that went well: the title says what happened with its particulars («240 € sent to Sam Lee»), the sentence what happens next, the action moves on. A task of several steps never ends on a notice alone. A failure is a `Note` with `tone="error"`, never an empty state.

props.name: title
props.doc: The title of the empty state (text or markup).

props.name: description
props.doc: A sentence below the title.

props.name: action
props.doc: An action below the text (a button).

props.name: icon
props.doc: An icon above the title (decorative, `aria-hidden`).

props.name: titleClassName
props.doc: Classes for the title, in place of the default ones where they overlap.

props.name: fill
props.doc: The whole of a view: as tall as the region it is in, centred in it, with the margins of a page (24px).

Park UI (MIT) file-upload 102769c — recipe translated to Tailwind for @acaprino/sigrid (https://github.com/chakra-ui/park-ui/blob/102769c/packages/preset/src/recipes/file-upload.ts)

A zone that takes a file: dropped on it, or chosen with the system picker, so dragging is never the only way (WCAG
2.5.7). The look is the attachments zone's (Park's `file-upload` recipe): the raised sheet with l3 corners and a 2px
dashed border in the control colour that turns solid ink while a file is dragged over it (the accent is not for this,
R2), two lines of text and no upload icon (the words say it, R6), 96px tall so it is an easy target with a mouse and a
finger. Ark UI's FileUpload gives the real button that opens the picker, the input behind it (outside the
accessibility tree and the tab order, emptied before each choice so the same file can be chosen again) and the checks
of type, size and count; the drop is the toolkit's `useDropTarget` (a drag that starts in the page is left alone).
The words are the app's: the label (the button's name, the same while dragging or busy), the hint (its description),
the line while dragging and while busy, and the error under the zone. Busy, the button keeps its focus and ignores
clicks and drops, like a loading Button. No animation.

props.name: label
props.doc: The main line, and the name of the button that opens the picker: "Drop a file here, or choose one".

props.name: hint
props.doc: The second line, read as the button's description: what the zone takes ("CSV, up to 5 MB").

props.name: dropLabel
props.doc: The main line while a file is dragged over the zone ("Drop it here"); the label when absent.

props.name: onFiles
props.doc: The files chosen or dropped that pass the checks (one, unless `multiple`).

props.name: onRefuse
props.doc: The files that do not pass, each with its reason: the app says why in `error`.

props.name: accept
props.doc: The types taken, as MIME type → extensions: `{ 'text/csv': ['.csv'] }`. A file passes on its type or its extension.

props.name: maxFileBytes
props.doc: The largest file taken, in bytes.

props.name: multiple
props.doc: Several files at once.

props.name: busy
props.doc: Work under way on the file just taken: this line takes the label's place and is announced, the zone takes nothing.

props.name: error
props.doc: What went wrong, under the zone and announced at once; the border turns destructive.

props.name: ref
props.doc: The button that opens the picker: to give it focus again.

types.name: FileDropRefusal
types.doc: A file the zone did not take, and why. `file` is null for a dropped text or link, which is not a file.
